x: Gratte soon brought himself well into the limelight by recording fast time from his mark in the Under 19 event. As expected, he won the final later, and followed this up by winning the final of the 100 yds. handicap open to all members, and so accomplished a good double.

All the heats in the 100 yards handicap, open to members of the three competing clubs, were won by Belgrave men; Gratte, the young runner who had a double win at our last meeting, again proved the winner on this occasion, with Birnie and Hughes, another young runner of promise, filling the other places.

A team consisting of Tosh, Scrimshaw, Williams (J.S.), Powter, Gratte, Clemens, Kench, and Ford (A.J.) made up the club team. The start from Baker Street was not at all encouraging, as the rain was descending in torrents, accompanied by plenty of lightning and thunder.
Gratte, who breasted the tape an easy winner. In the 880 yards team race (4 to start and 3 to score) we were represented by F.
